brief: Sprout, a plant-care reminder app: why users churned and what would win them back
questions: Why did you stop using the Sprout plant-care app?
What would bring you back to the app?

respondents.name: Ava Lindqvist
answers: The monthly subscription was too expensive for what I got.
Nothing really, I have moved on.

respondents.name: Ben Okafor
answers: It sent me way too many reminders and I started ignoring them.
Let me choose how often it reminds me and I would come back.

respondents.name: Carla Mendes
answers: I switched to a simple spreadsheet that does the same thing for free. It also crashed a lot.
Fix the crashes and I would give it another go.

respondents.name: Dev Raman
answers: The constant pings every morning drove me up the wall.
A cheaper plan, or a one-time purchase, would get me to return.

respondents.name: Elena Petrov
answers: I just did not have the time to log everything anymore.
If I could group the reminders into one daily summary, that would help.

respondents.name: Frank Dubois
answers: I could not justify paying $12 a month to remind me to water a fern.
If it could identify a plant from a photo reliably, I would be back.

respondents.name: Grace Tanaka
answers: The app kept crashing whenever I opened my plant list.
If the subscription dropped to a few dollars a month I would come back.

respondents.name: Hugo Silva
answers: It cost more than I wanted to spend on a hobby, so I canceled.
If it stopped losing my data I would return.

respondents.name: Imani Brooks
answers: I got a notification for every single plant, every single day.
I do not think anything would, I do not need it anymore.

respondents.name: Jonas Weber
answers: A friend showed me a different plant app that I liked better.
Bring back the free tier with the basics and I am in.

respondents.name: Kira Novak
answers: The alerts were so frequent that I muted the app entirely.
A stable version that does not freeze would be enough.

respondents.name: Leo Castillo
answers: Work got busy and updating the app became a chore I skipped. The reminders were relentless too.
Probably nothing, my plants are fine without it.

respondents.name: Mia Johansson
answers: The price kept going up and I finally decided it was not worth it.
An option to set quiet hours and fewer alerts would bring me back.

respondents.name: Noah Kim
answers: It froze on me constantly and I lost my watering log twice.
Better plant identification would be a big draw for me.

respondents.name: Olive Grant
answers: Honestly it was the subscription fee. I did not want another monthly charge.
I would return if there was a lower yearly fee.

respondents.name: Pablo Ortiz
answers: My photos would not upload and the app was glitchy all the time.
Only remind me when a plant is actually thirsty, not on a fixed schedule.

respondents.name: Quinn Harper
answers: I moved to a paper notebook, it works better for me.
I would return if the photo recognition stopped mixing up my succulents.

respondents.name: Rosa Alvarez
answers: Too many buzzes on my phone, so I turned it all off and forgot about it.
A discount for long-time users would do it.

respondents.name: Sam Patel
answers: With two kids I could not keep up with entering every plant.
I would come back once syncing between devices works properly.

respondents.name: Tara Ng
answers: For a bit of watering help the cost felt silly, so I dropped it.
I am not planning to come back.

respondents.name: Uma Reddy
answers: I stopped because my schedule got packed and I forgot to open it.
Make it affordable and I will reinstall it tomorrow.

respondents.name: Victor Hale
answers: Paying every month for something I barely opened seemed wasteful.
Make the app run smoothly and I will try it again.

respondents.name: Wendy Cho
answers: Syncing between my phone and tablet never worked, it was buggy.
Nothing, I am happy with how things are now.

respondents.name: Xavier Moreau
answers: Another app had a nicer layout, so I moved over to that one.
Smarter reminders that skip days after rain or watering would do it.

respondents.name: Yara Haddad
answers: I was getting reminder after reminder, even for plants I had just watered.
Accurate disease diagnosis from a picture would bring me back.

respondents.name: Zane Fischer
answers: Life got hectic and tracking my plants fell off my list.
A free plan with unlimited plants would win me back.

respondents.name: Alma Rossi
answers: It got too expensive after the free trial ended.
A weekly digest instead of daily pings would be perfect.

respondents.name: Bruno Costa
answers: I did not have spare minutes to maintain the app every week.
A feature that tells me what is wrong with a sick leaf would do it.

respondents.name: Chloe Evans
answers: The yearly fee was more than I wanted to pay.
Less money per month, that is all it would take.

respondents.name: Dario Greco
answers: After the last update it crashed every time I launched it.
No more bugs, that is my only condition.
